gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Exodus 1200's '1,500 W boost mode' is not continuous power. When The Solar Lab ran a 1,500 W heat gun on it, the unit gave about 1,300 W for roughly 5 minutes. The same reviewers could not get its AC charging above 400 W and needed more than 4 hours to fill it. The Mega 1 takes 1,400 W from the wall alone, and its '36-minute' full charge needs that plus 800 W of solar (2,200 W).
standout_why: I compared five pages. ShopSavvy (Exodus 1200) gives 1,200 W, a 3,600 W surge and 'about 2.5 hours' from the wall, but no input watts. Active Gear Review (Exodus 1200, Jan 2025) gives 1,500 W boost, 3,600 W surge, 3,500 cycles to 80% and '0–80% in 72 minutes', with no measured numbers. Make Tech Easier (old 1100W, archived) gives a 3,200 W peak and a 6.5-hour AC charge. Nerdtechy (old 1100W) gives 3,600 cycles 'before it loses 10 percent'. OUPES's own collection and off-grid pages list only Wh and W, with no surge or cycle figures. None of them separates boost from rated output, measures AC charging, or says the Mega 1's headline charge time counts AC plus solar.
decides: This backs the Mega 1 as the OUPES pick near 1 kWh. Its 2,000 W rated output covers 1,500 W heaters and kettles outright, where the Exodus 1200 relies on a boost that measured about 1,300 W. It also recharges from the wall at up to 1,400 W, against under 400 W measured for the Exodus 1200. In The Solar Lab's full-load runs the two delivered similar shares of their rating (79% vs 77%). The battery ratings don't separate the current models: every one is rated to 80% capacity (3,500+ or 4,000+ cycles). The Exodus 1200 is also marked Sold Out on oupes.com. The $599 Mega 1 Lite lists the same 1,400 W AC input and 800 W solar input as the $699 Mega 1.

findings.label: Boost mode measured with a 1,500 W heat gun
findings.value: about 1,300 W for about 5 minutes (rated 1,200 W, advertised 1,500 W boost)
findings.source_title: OUPES Exodus 1200 Review: Good Deal or Complete Failure? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab: there is no button or app setting for boost mode. The unit handles quick spikes but shuts off quickly when its rating is exceeded. The page gives no reviewer name or date.

findings.label: AC charging, spec vs measured
findings.value: spec 300–600 W; measured under 400 W in Fast Charging mode; over 4 h to full
findings.source_title: OUPES Exodus 1200 Review: Good Deal or Complete Failure? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: This conflicts with Active Gear Review's '0% to 80% in 72 minutes' (a feature claim they did not measure) and ShopSavvy's 'about 2.5 hours'. OUPES's US listing gives only '840W Max. Input charging speed (AC + Solar)'.

findings.label: Delivered share of rated capacity at full load
findings.value: about 77% at a 1,198 W load (38.5 min vs 49.5 min ideal), about 763 Wh of 992 Wh
findings.source_title: OUPES Exodus 1200 Review: Good Deal or Complete Failure? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: Wh is my arithmetic: 992 × 38.5 / 49.5 ≈ 772 Wh by runtime ratio, or 992 × 0.77 ≈ 764 Wh using the rounded %. About 78% at a load roughly 100 W lower.

findings.label: US maker listing and price
findings.value: $549 (compare-at $799); 1,200 W rated, 1,500 W boost; 3,500+ cycles to 80%; title marked '(Sold Out)'
findings.source_title: (Sold Out) OUPES Exodus 1200 Portable Power Station | 1200W 992Wh
findings.note: Read with storecheck.py search on oupes.com (Shopify data). The product page itself returned HTTP 429. The listing text gives a boost figure but no surge figure.

findings.label: AC input alone vs headline charge speed
findings.value: 1,400 W max AC (90–140 V, 12 A); solar 800 W max (12–78 V, 14 A); '36 min' full charge is quoted with '2200W Max. Input', i.e. AC 1,400 W + solar 800 W
findings.note: AC and solar limits come from the manual's spec page. The 36 min / 2,200 W wording comes from the oupes.com listing (next finding). 1,400 + 800 = 2,200, my arithmetic. The manual also gives 'Max 2000W (Surge: 4500W)' and a 20 ms EPS switchover.

findings.note: Read with storecheck.py search on oupes.com. The listing says 'Fastest Charging Speed: Fully charge in 36 mins 2200W Max. Input charging speed'.

findings.label: Delivered share of rated capacity at near-full load
findings.value: 79% at a sustained 1,779 W load (27 min), about 809 Wh of 1,024 Wh
findings.source_title: OUPES Mega 1 Review: Affordable and Powerful or Too Good to Be True? (The Solar Lab)

findings.label: AC input and charge time, US maker listing
findings.value: $599 (compare-at $1,329); 100% in 46 min via 1,400 W AC input; 800 W max solar (69 min); 2,000 W / 4,500 W surge; 3,500+ cycles to 80%

findings.label: Cycle-life basis across rival pages
findings.value: Current OUPES listings all rate to 80% capacity (3,500+ cycles: Mega 1/1 Lite/2/3, Exodus 1200; 4,000+: Exodus 350/700, Guardian 6000 V2). Nerdtechy's '3,600 cycles before it loses 10 percent' is for the discontinued 1100W.
findings.note: The 80% figures come from the oupes.com listings cited in the findings above. Nerdtechy's 90% basis is not the same measure as the 80% ratings, so don't compare the counts directly.
